title: Let the AI cook | ivan.codes
excerpt: AI coding works when the stack is right and the developer has the experience to trust the output. Most of the elaborate workflows being shared are people getting in their own way.
content_html:
I keep seeing posts where somebody walks through the elaborate workflow they figured out for getting AI to write production code, and the workflow gets way more credit than it deserves. The two things doing the work are the stack the model is writing into and whatever the developer has built up over their career: taste, pattern recognition, a feel for which way the code wants to go. Everything on top of those two is decoration.

What I hear from people trying to follow those workflows usually sounds something like this:

Spent an hour on this and Claude still couldn't get it right. I gave it the whole file, listed every edge case, told it exactly which function to touch, specified the naming convention. It still messed it up.

In cases like this the prompt itself is the problem, because each constraint added to it narrows what the model can do, and by the time you've stacked five or six the field of view is small enough that the model has to thread a needle through whatever assumptions you packed in along the way. Any time one of those assumptions is wrong, and at least one usually is, the output looks like a failure even though the model was doing exactly what you asked.

My version is usually two turns. The first one points the agent at context I already have locally, the second one says what to build:

Both work because the priming step alone ticks a bunch of boxes the over-prompter is trying to hit one at a time. Once the agent has read the reference it already matches the conventions, the naming patterns, the way functions are structured, and how errors get handled, all the stuff people otherwise try to spell out constraint by constraint.

Once you accept the model can write the code, you're left with a choice about how to work with it. That's where most devs shoot themselves in the foot. Letting the model run feels like giving up control, while inventing a workflow feels like the responsible move, even when it produces worse work in more time.

The reason that feels like losing control runs deeper than the code itself. Devs have spent twenty years tying their sense of worth to what they produced, whether that was a clever solution, an abstraction nobody else saw, or the late-night fix that finally worked, and all of it was how the industry measured you and how you measured yourself. When a model arrives that can produce the artifact for you, often a better one, inventing a new layer of work it can't do yet is how you keep being at the center of things, but the layer keeps shrinking, and the people who can't let go end up spending more and more of their time on ceremony that exists so they can still feel essential.

What's left for the developer is the harder part of the job, which is picking the stack, having the taste, and catching the moment the output starts to drift, and the elaborate process layered around all of that is mostly busywork that lets you feel productive while you avoid the harder, vaguer thing.

Let the AI cook.

content_html_zh:
我不断看到一些帖子，其中有人介绍了他们为让人工智能编写生产代码而设计的复杂工作流程，而该工作流程得到的信任远远超出了应有的程度。 完成工作的两件事是模型正在写入的堆栈以及开发人员在其职业生涯中建立的任何内容：品味、模式识别、对代码想要走向的感觉。 这两者之上的所有东西都是装饰。

我从尝试遵循这些工作流程的人们那里听到的通常听起来像这样：

克劳德花了一个小时，还是没有搞清楚。 我给了它整个文件，列出了每个边缘情况，准确地告诉它要触摸哪个函数，指定了命名约定。 结果还是把事情搞砸了。

在这种情况下，提示本身就是问题，因为添加到它的每个约束都会缩小模型可以做的事情，当你堆叠了五六个时，视野已经足够小，模型必须通过你一路上打包的任何假设。 每当这些假设之一错误（通常至少有一个错误）时，即使模型完全按照您的要求进行操作，输出也会看起来失败。

我的版本通常是两圈。 第一个将代理指向我本地已有的上下文，第二个说明要构建什么：

两者都有效，因为启动步骤本身就勾选了一堆盒子，而过度提示器试图一次点击一个。 一旦代理读取了引用，它就已经匹配了约定、命名模式、函数的构造方式以及错误的处理方式，以及人们试图通过约束逐个阐明约束的所有内容。

一旦您接受模型可以编写代码，您就可以选择如何使用它。 这就是大多数开发者搬起石头砸自己脚的地方。 让模型运行感觉就像放弃控制权，而发明工作流程感觉像是负责任的举动，即使它在更长的时间内产生了更糟糕的工作。

感觉失去控制的原因比代码本身更深层次。 开发人员花了二十年的时间将他们的价值感与他们所生产的产品联系在一起，无论这是一个聪明的解决方案，一个没人见过的抽象概念，还是最终起作用的深夜修复，所有这一切都是行业如何衡量你以及你如何衡量自己的。 当一个模型出现时，可以为你生产出工件，通常是更好的工件，发明一层它还无法完成的新工作，你就可以一直处于事物的中心，但这一层不断缩小，而那些无法放手的人最终会花越来越多的时间在存在的仪式上，这样他们仍然可以感到自己是重要的。

留给开发人员的是工作中更困难的部分，即挑选堆栈、品味并捕捉输出开始漂移的时刻，而围绕所有这些的复杂流程主要是忙碌的工作，让您在避免更困难、更模糊的事情的同时感到高效。

让人工智能做饭。
